Title: Who Stole My Peanuts?
Author: by Cathy Andrews Hinman
Content: “Can we ride our bikes to Birch's Store?” asked Patty as Dad turned into the campground. “I want to buy peanuts in the shells.”
Mama smiled. “After we set up camp.”
At the gate, Patty's brother asked, “Can we ride our bikes in?” “Sure,” said Dad.
Patty and Cody grabbed their helmets and bikes from the truck and sped through the gate. Patty inhaled the woodsy scent of pine needles. “I love this place.”
“Me too!” Cody passed Patty.
Cody always arrived `text(first)`, no matter where they went. “Let's get things set up so we can go to Birch's.”

Patty's heart raced as she wound the twinkle lights around a tree. She and Cody helped pitch the tent and set up the cots. She liked sleeping in the tent where she could smell campfires and frying bacon in the morning. At night, her lights eased the eerie sounds of swaying branches and dropping pinecones. She tried not to think about wildlife at night, but she knew Mama and Dad slept right beside her.

ZZZZZIP! “All done!” said Patty.
“Can we go to Birch's now?”
“OK,” Mama said.

Patty smelled apple-cinnamon as she opened Birch's door. She ran to the big wooden barrels with signs: Salted, Unsalted. “They still have them!” She scooped salted peanuts into a plastic bag until the scale read `text(one pound)`.
“Geez, Patty,” said Cody. “Do you have enough peanuts? That bag is as big as my football!”
Patty grinned. “You want me to share, don't you?”
“Come on, kids,” said Mama, “let's go swimming.”

Cody zoomed ahead and stood dressed in his swim trunks when Patty arrived. Her mouth watered as she opened her bag. The salty nutshell dried her mouth. “Umm!” She took the soaked shell from her mouth and broke it with her fingers. Patty popped `text(two)` peanuts into her mouth.
“Can I have some?” asked Cody.
“Sure, everyone can have some. When they're gone, we'll go to Birch's again.”

Mama and Dad laughed and grabbed their towels. Patty spun her bag of peanuts, set it on the table, and tucked the twisted stem under the bag. By the time she straddled her bike, Cody had already rounded the beach corner. After swimming, they rode back to their campsite. When Patty pulled in, Cody was sitting near the table. Patty gasped at her plastic bag full of air!
“Who stole my peanuts?”
“Not me,” said Cody, shaking his head.
“Somebody stole my peanuts!” cried Patty.
“What?” Mama stared at Cody. He shook his head. “Patty, is this a prank so you can go to Birch's again?”
“No!” cried Patty.
Dad parked his bike. “You'll figure it out.”
Patty looked to the left.
An older couple, she thought. They probably wouldn't like peanuts. She looked at the campers to the right who were tending a baby. No, they wouldn't give peanuts to a baby.
Cody stuffed chips into his mouth and spilled some on the ground.
“Don't be such a slob,” said Patty. “You're not supposed to leave open food around. It draws the animals.” She held her empty bag. “Why would somebody steal my peanuts without the bag?”
“Yeah,” said Cody. “They'd snatch the whole bag and run.”
Patty rubbed her chin. She saw something from the corner of her eye.
“Mystery solved! I know who stole my peanuts!”
“Who?” asked Cody.
Patty pointed under Cody's chair. “He must have worked fast to shell a `text(pound)` of peanuts.”
Cody laughed. “I guess he's stocking up for `text(winter)`!”
Mama smiled. “Back to Birch's.”
